scope: One bounded 24-cell policy-enforcement model: three same-repository authority surfaces x eight adversarial/interruption events. No live policy mutation was performed. Evidence is limited to own clean continuation plus current official GitHub documentation.

observations: Protected branches are available for public repositories on GitHub Free; private-repository availability depends on paid plans.
Branch protection blocks force pushes and branch deletion by default.
By default those restrictions do not apply to repository admins or custom roles with bypass-branch-protections permission; GitHub allows applying restrictions to them too.
Repository admins or custom roles with edit-repository-rules permission can create, edit, and delete repository rulesets.
Rulesets can restrict branch/tag deletion and block force pushes; bypass actors may be configured.
Rulesets are available for public repositories on GitHub Free; private/internal availability is plan-dependent, and some push-ruleset cases require GitHub Team.
Repository admins or organization owners can delete a repository unless a higher-level organization or enterprise policy prevents it.
Repository deletion is therefore outside the enforcement power of repository-local branch protection/rulesets themselves.

policies.unprotected_ref_plus_blob_CAS: Authority state lives on an ordinary repository ref; claim writes use current-blob CAS/readback.
policies.protected_branch_default_plus_blob_CAS: Default branch protection blocks ordinary force-push/delete but default admin bypass semantics remain; claim writes use current-blob CAS/readback.
policies.admin_enforced_or_empty_bypass_ruleset_p: Direct force-push/delete is blocked even for normal admin/bypass paths where configured, but repository admins/edit-rules roles can still change/delete repository-local rulesets and repository admins/owners can delete the repository; claim writes use current-blob CAS/readback.

observation_vs_inference.observed_from_docs: GitHub repository-level protections can block force pushes/deletions, but repository admins/edit-rules roles can edit/delete rulesets, default branch protection exempts admins unless explicitly included, and repository admins/owners can delete repositories unless prevented by a higher-level policy.
observation_vs_inference.model_inference: A same-repository freshness/retirement witness cannot be called non-rewindable against an authority that can both weaken repository-local policy and destroy the repository containing the witness. Stronger branch protection closes direct-ref mutation but not the meta-policy/repository-lifecycle channel.
observation_vs_inference.scope_guard: This does not prove impossibility against every GitHub account/organization design. It falsifies the narrower candidate in which the non-rewind proof is entirely repository-local while repository-level administrators or owners remain in the threat model.

retry_and_claim_result.stale_claimant: Current-blob CAS remains sufficient only while repository identity/history has not been authoritatively rewound or replaced.
retry_and_claim_result.response_loss: A deterministic claim path plus exact readback can convert unknown response into committed/not-committed classification without duplicating the same repository effect.
retry_and_claim_result.rate_limit: Fail closed and checkpoint across invocations; rate limit is an availability interruption, not authority to retry blindly or accept stale state.
retry_and_claim_result.concurrency: Same-object current-blob CAS gives one-winner conflict behavior for concurrent writers, but does not itself provide anti-rewind history.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.public_repository_free_scope: Protected branches and repository rulesets are documented as available on GitHub Free for public repositories; no finite hosted-compute credit is needed for the policy check itself.
zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.generic_private_repository_scope: Plan/visibility dependence exists for protected branches/rulesets in private repositories, so a generic paid-plan-independent acceptance claim is not established.

result.new_narrowing: Repository-local protection can close direct branch rewind, but it cannot be a non-bypassable monotonic freshness boundary when an in-scope repository admin/rules editor can weaken that protection or an admin/owner can delete the repository. The remaining useful candidate is privilege-domain separation: all recurring workers must lack policy/lifecycle authority, and a durable identity/freshness check must survive credential rotation and repository replacement without relying on an external hosted coordinator.
result.minimal_unresolved_child: Can least-privileged worker credentials plus a stable repository-identity fence make claim/effect authority safe against worker-originated rewind/delete while explicitly failing closed on owner/admin policy or repository-lifecycle changes, with public-free/zero-quota operation and no external monotonic witness?

continuation: Part122: execute one bounded least-privilege authority-separation model. Compare worker token/App permissions limited to contents, worker credentials with administration, and repository-owner lifecycle authority across force-push, rule edit/delete, repository delete/recreate, token rotation/revocation, stale claimant, response-loss retry, and rate-limit interruption. Require a stable repository-identity check and fail closed on identity/policy uncertainty. Determine whether narrowing the threat model to worker-originated effects yields a zero-cost public-free repository-local candidate without claiming safety against owner/admin compromise; persist one checkpoint and no second leaf.
